claim: [L668-L682] (HIGH/nontermination/numerical-domain) The backward-distance loop divides by an unchecked average wavelength and has no progress guard, so zero or nonpositive dsc or L1 can make disfac invalid or leave backdis unchanged indefinitely.
other_wording: [L672-L682] (HIGH/nontermination) The backtracking loop has no guard for zero dsc or zero/invalid averaged L1, so disfac can be zero and backdis can fail to advance indefinitely.

claim: [L293-L339, L570-L574] (HIGH/wrong-destination) The wavenumber source is copied into cobs instead of kobs, after which uninitialized kobs values drive the celerity residual and uncertainty calculations.

claim: [L687-L706] (HIGH/singular-wave-derivative) Hb and dHbdh divide by k and by sinh(kh) times cosh(kh) plus kh without protecting the common zero-k or zero-kh limit.
other_wording: [L688-L705] (MED/singular-formula) Hb and its derivative divide by or evaluate singular hyperbolic ratios at s%k or kh without a positive lower bound, so zero-wavenumber cells can generate invalid values.

claim: [L15-L39, L484-L485] (HIGH/pointer-state) Pointer components have no default NULL initialization, yet ASSOCIATED is called on fobs1 before any guaranteed association-status definition.

[L476-L487, L527-L548] (HIGH/input-validation/indexing) Observation-grid dimensions and spacings are used for allocation, division, MOD, and indices that assume nx and ny are at least three without validating positive dx, dy, nx, or ny.

[L264-L335] (HIGH/numerical-domain) Celerity and wavenumber calculations divide by unchecked tradar, hh, rk, and rk plus sigK and are evaluated over dry cells before any wet-cell guard.

[L753-L756, L774] (HIGH/zero-denominator) The weighting and depth-correction formulas lack guards for zero combined variance and for the all-zero dDdh case, where the latter evaluates an explicit zero-over-zero.

[L208-L219, L248-L269] (MED/limit-inconsistency) Update-time friction omits the initialization-time mincf lower clamp, and the grain-size u branch uniquely hard-caps at 0.1 instead of maxcf, producing direction- and timestep-dependent bounds.
other_wording: [L90-L103, L208-L219] (MED/inconsistent-clamping) Manning friction is clamped to both mincf and maxcf at initialization but only to maxcf during updates, allowing the advertised lower bound to be lost after the first update.

claim: [L196-L205] (HIGH/parameter-division) Dynamic Manning roughness divides by dstem and droot without requiring either configured length scale to be nonzero.
other_wording: [L198-L205] (LOW/division-precondition) Dynamic Manning roughness divides by dstem and droot with no local nonzero check, leaving its parameter contract implicit.

claim: [L70-L72, L104-L164, L220-L272] (HIGH/numerical-domain) Chezy and White-Colebrook formulas divide by unchecked bed-friction or roughness coefficients and take logarithms derived from them, allowing zero or nonpositive input to produce invalid coefficients.
other_wording: [L104-L164, L220-L272] (LOW/roughness-precondition) White-Colebrook formulas divide by kru/krv and take log10 without locally enforcing positive roughness heights, so validity depends entirely on upstream input constraints.

claim: [L357-L378, L398-L418] (HIGH/numerical-domain) The infiltration enhancement divides by cfu or cfv twice without a positive lower-bound guard, which is unsafe for zero-valued constant-friction configurations.

[L365-L373, L406-L414] (LOW/zero-input-bias) Exactly zero infiltration is forced to a nonzero negative blphi and therefore a facbl slightly different from one, so the nominally absent process still adds shear.
[L701-L727] (MED/directional-bias) Using SIGN with zero velocity assigns positive turbulent bed shear at rest, introducing a fixed directional bias wherever kbl is positive.

[L41-L62] (HIGH/MPI-ownership/reduction) Every rank whose local index test succeeds advances the drifter, while idrift and jdrift are reduced independently with MPI_MIN, so overlapping ownership or differing local updates can select coordinates from different ranks and create a position no rank computed.
other_wording: [L53-L62] (MED/distributed-state-consistency) MPI_MIN is applied independently to idrift and jdrift, so if different overlapping ranks produce the minima the reduced coordinate pair need not come from any single rank's drifter update.

claim: [L360-L366, L760-L766, L785-L791, L806-L807, L922-L930] (HIGH/grid-metric/indexing) Multiple two-dimensional correction formulas hard-code the transverse metric index to 1 even though neighboring code uses the current i or j, making the scheme inconsistent on spatially varying curvilinear grids.
other_wording: [L359-L366] (MED/grid-metric-indexing) Cross-advection of v uses s%dsu(...,1) throughout a two-dimensional loop and the first negative-flow gradient uses dsu(ie,1) for the i-to-ie interval, which is inconsistent with local curvilinear spacing.

other_wording: [L49-L80, L157-L160] (LOW/lifecycle-contract) Module work arrays are allocated once with the first grid shape and have no reinitialization or shape check, so repeated library initialization with a different grid would retain incompatible storage.

claim: [L784-L792] (HIGH/numerical-sign) The negative-v qy continuity branch omits the sign reversal used by the corresponding negative-u branch and by the other second-order flux routines, yielding a correction with the opposite sign.
other_wording: [L784-L792] (HIGH/sign-inconsistency) The negative-v continuity correction lacks the leading minus used by the analogous negative-u branch, making the qy correction's sign inconsistent with the qx implementation.

claim: [L74-L122,L635-L656,L645-L652,L767-L771] (MED/state/configuration lifecycle) Old-state arrays are allocated only if second-order or nonhydrostatic mode is active on the first call, so enabling either mode later accesses unallocated storage; all saved work arrays also retain the first grid shape.
other_wording: [L74-L92, L767-L771] (MED/conditional-allocation) Old-state arrays are allocated only if second-order or nonhydrostatic mode is active on the first call; because later allocation is gated by vsu, enabling either mode on a reused instance would access unallocated uu_old, vv_old, and zs_old.

claim: [L621-L627] (MED/boundary-condition mapping) The physical left boundary passes par%right to flow_lat_bc while the physical right boundary passes par%left, an unexplained reversal of boundary configuration.
other_wording: [L618-L627] (HIGH/boundary-condition-selection) The left global boundary calls flow_lat_bc with par%right while the right global boundary passes par%left, apparently swapping the configured lateral boundary types.

claim: [L512-L526] (HIGH/wrong wet-mask component) The Smagorinsky cross-stress mask for V momentum multiplies three wetu values but uses wetv(i-1,j) for the fourth point, inconsistent with the U-velocity stencil.

claim: [L776-L794,L805-L853,L866-L936] (HIGH/stale interpolation boundaries) Multiple cell/face interpolants (vu, vsu, usu, uv, vsv, usv, ue, and ve) leave MPI-internal halo rows/columns or nx+1/ny+1 edges unset, as the inline comments acknowledge, yet whole-array velocity magnitudes consume them.

claim: [L365-L369,L471-L478,L593-L617] (MED/stale disabled-viscosity component) The viscosity-off branch clears nuh and viscu but not viscv, so a runtime transition from enabled to disabled viscosity leaves the prior V-viscous acceleration active.

claim: [L956-L972] (MED/singular profile inputs) The vertical-profile call derives ks using sqrt(g/cfu) without ensuring positive cfu and passes potentially zero sigm/k values into a routine that divides by both.
other_wording: [L956-L972] (LOW/roughness-location-contract) The cell-centered vertical-profile call derives ks directly from u-point cfu(i,j) without documenting interpolation or guarding the positive-friction prerequisite.

claim: [L1349-L1436,L1575-L1613] (MED/unbounded nonlinear iteration) Turbulent conductivity iterations have no iteration limit or non-finite/stagnation exit.
other_wording: [L1349-L1436] (MED/unbounded-iteration) All turbulent conductivity fixed-point loops have no iteration cap or non-finite escape even though maxiter is declared elsewhere in the module, so a nonconvergent cell can stall the timestep.

claim: [L836-L905,L913-L917,L1001-L1005,L1016-L1019,L1103-L1105] (HIGH/zero aquifer-height singularity) The exponential head formulation repeatedly evaluates sinh(h)/h at cells whose groundwater height can be zero, without a limiting-form implementation or mask.

claim: [L1567-L1642] (MED/zero timestep/porosity/progress denominator) Local infiltration divides by dt, porosity, twodtp, dis, and infiltration rate without explicit guards, so zero conductivity or invalid timestep/porosity can cause singular intermediate arithmetic.
other_wording: [L1568-L1643] (MED/division-by-zero) Local infiltration divides by dt/por and later by dis and infil without guarding zero conductivity, zero timestep, zero porosity, or a zero computed infiltration distance.

claim: [L734-L738] (MED/zero smoothing thickness) The wet-layer ratio divides by dwetlayer with no positive-value guard.
other_wording: [L724-L739, L1478-L1513] (MED/zero-transition-width) dwetlayer is used as a divisor in both the smoothing ratio and hydrostatic infiltration cap without a local positive-width check.

claim: [L976-L1009] (HIGH/wrong loop variable/index) The fast 2-D exponential solver loops on k but never sets i, so it uses stale/zero i to index all grid fields and metrics.
other_wording: [L976-L1009] (HIGH/wrong-loop-index) The fast 2-D exponential solver loops on k but never sets i, then uses the initialized value i=0 in grid and coefficient subscripts, causing invalid indexing.

claim: [L1025-L1106] (HIGH/missing solver implementation) The full 2-D branch builds and solves a matrix only for the parabolic model; selecting exponential skips the solve and then computes gwhead from stale gwcurv.
other_wording: [L1025-L1106] (HIGH/unimplemented-selection) The full 2-D solver builds and solves coefficients only for the parabolic model, but afterward accepts the exponential model and computes a head from gwcurv that this branch never solved.

other_wording: [L1011-L1020] (HIGH/shape-mismatch) The fast 2-D solver assigns x(:,1), sized nx+1, into gwhead(2:nx,j), sized nx-1, in both head-model branches.

claim: [L940-L975] (HIGH/out-of-bounds matrix index) The fast 2-D parabolic solver loops on i but writes A and rhs at index k, which remains initialized to zero, causing second-dimension index-zero accesses.
other_wording: [L938-L975] (HIGH/out-of-bounds-index) The fast 2-D parabolic solver loops on i but indexes A and rhs with k, which remains zero from line 817, causing index-zero writes.

claim: [L1203-L1265] (HIGH/wrong directional conductivity/metric) Both v-interface infiltration calls pass Kx instead of Ky, and the first v-interface surface-water availability limit uses dsz where the surrounding v-direction scaling uses dnz.
other_wording: [L1203-L1235] (MED/directional-metric-inconsistency) The v-interface infiltration availability limit uses s%hh*s%dsz for the surface-water volume while the groundwater side and all v-direction area scaling use dnz, creating an x/y metric mismatch.

claim: [L607-L612,L1349-L1436,L1811-L1816] (MED/unchecked enum output) Several scheme/model SELECT CASE blocks have no default, so unsupported gwscheme or head-model values leave logicals or result/output variables undefined.
other_wording: [L607-L612, L1349-L1436, L1811-L1816] (LOW/enum-validation) Several select-case blocks have no default assignment, so an unsupported groundwater scheme or head model can leave logicals or numeric outputs undefined unless validation is guaranteed upstream.

claim: [L655-L721,L1308-L1323] (HIGH/uninitialized MPI interface boundary) gwhu(nx+1,:) and gwhv(:,ny+1) are assigned only on physical bottom/right ranks, yet velocity and flux loops consume all nx+1 by ny+1 entries on internal MPI ranks.

claim: [L2185-L2198] (HIGH/relative-density formula) intra_sedtr defines ratio_s=(rhos-rho)/rho and then uses ratio_s-1 in dstar, subtracting unity twice relative to the submerged-density ratio used elsewhere.

claim: [L70-L138,L619-L630,L1218-L1226,L1361-L1433,L1886-L1942,L2536-L2619,L2863-L2871,L3013-L3030,L3086-L3095,L3183-L3187,L3235-L3238] (LOW/state/dimension lifecycle) Many saved work arrays are allocated only on first use and never resized or reconfigured, so changed grid, grain, layer, or formulation settings in a later lifecycle retain incompatible state.
other_wording: [L70-L138, L619-L630, L1361-L1433, L1886-L1942, L2536-L2619] (LOW/lifecycle-contract) Multiple saved workspaces are allocated once from the first grid and option set with no shape or option-change checks, making library reuse with changed configuration unsafe.

other_wording: [L1886-L1916] (HIGH/unallocated-access) Nielsen2006 allocates fe only when streaming is enabled but assigns fe=0 unconditionally, accessing an unallocated array when streaming is off.

other_wording: [L3032-L3036] (MED/zero-wavenumber-singularity) The Ursell number divides by (k*hh)^3 before applying its lower clamp, so zero k or depth yields non-finite intermediate values.

other_wording: [L1664-L1682] (MED/signed-concentration) Van Rijn 1993 activates bed load using nonnegative speed ue but computes and divides by signed used=vmg+ua, allowing negative or singular equilibrium concentration.

other_wording: [L819-L830] (MED/unit-inconsistency) During groundwater-coupled erosion tempexchange is a water-depth amount but is added directly to the infiltration rate without division by dt, unlike the accretion branch.

claim: [L1218-L1226] (HIGH/heterogeneous-layer bounds) update_fractions sizes scratch arrays from s%nd(1,1) but indexes them using each target cell's nd and par%nd_var, which can overrun when layer counts vary spatially.
other_wording: [L1218-L1226] (MED/workspace-shape) update_fractions sizes saved work arrays from nd(1,1) and never checks the current cell's nd(i,j), so spatially varying layer counts can exceed or mismatch the workspace.

claim: [L1752-L1756] (MED/unchecked vertical resolution) The concentration grid divides by kmax-1 and therefore requires kmax>=2 without checking that contract.
other_wording: [L1752-L1756] (MED/configuration-singularity) The vertical integration grid divides by kmax-1, so kmax=1 is unsupported without an explicit parameter guard.

claim: [L437-L453] (MED/angle/quadrant handling) Talmon direction calculations use atan of component ratios rather than atan2, including a possible zero denominator and loss of the correct quadrant for the adjusted transport direction.
other_wording: [L437-L453, L1557-L1578] (MED/angle-singularity) Transport and slope directions use atan(y/x) with manual quadrant handling and still divide by zero for vertical vectors, rather than a two-argument angle function.

claim: [L360-L366] (HIGH/dry-face division) The Surfbeat berm-slope mask evaluates H/hu across the full grid without a wet or positive-depth guard.
other_wording: [L357-L373] (MED/division-before-mask) The Surfbeat berm-slope condition evaluates H/hu across the array without protecting zero hu before the logical selection.

claim: [L1234-L1240] (HIGH/nonterminating exact-residual loop) The fraction update loops until a floating residual is exactly zero and can make zero progress when a limiting layer thickness is zero, with no tolerance or iteration cap.
other_wording: [L1218-L1239, L1318] (HIGH/nontermination) update_fractions loops until an exact floating-point zero and has no escape when dzbt becomes zero because a limiting layer thickness is zero, so dzb_loc may never decrease.

claim: [L2943-L2956] (HIGH/uninitialized sink term) In 2-D turbulence advection, disturb is used after the betad<=0 branch where its only assignment is commented out.
other_wording: [L2943-L2956] (HIGH/uninitialized-variable) In 2-D turbulence advection disturb is assigned only when betad>0 but is used unconditionally in the kturb update, leaving it undefined for betad<=0.

claim: [L2282-L2303] (HIGH/unguarded concentration division/stale output) ceqbg is formed by dividing bed transport by hh*uu before the low-shear mask is applied, and the bed-disabled branch clears Subg but not ceqbg.
other_wording: [L2282-L2291] (HIGH/division-before-mask) intra_sedtr computes ceqbg by dividing Subg by hh*uu before zeroing subcritical transport, so zero velocities generate NaN or infinity that the later Subg mask does not remove from ceqbg.

claim: [L2431-L2473] (HIGH/singular concentration integration) Suspended concentration divides by hh-za and hh without ensuring water depth exceeds the reference height or is positive.
other_wording: [L2442-L2473] (MED/concentration-singularity) The analytical concentration profile divides by hh-za and the final depth average divides by hh without handling the hh=za or zero-depth limits.

claim: [L290-L307] (HIGH/nonconformable array assignment) At the right MPI boundary, uev_sed(:,1:ny+1)=uev_sed(:,1:ny) assigns arrays with different extents instead of assigning only the final column.
other_wording: [L290-L298] (HIGH/shape-mismatch) At a right MPI boundary uev_sed(:,1:ny+1) is assigned from uev_sed(:,1:ny), a nonconformable array assignment that appears intended to copy only the final column.

claim: [L225-L237] (HIGH/uninitialized boundary values) With nz>1, ueu_sed and veu_sed are filled only through nx, while whole-array velocity magnitudes immediately consume their nx+1 boundary; non-bottom MPI ranks do not initialize that boundary.
other_wording: [L225-L237, L290-L307] (MED/partial-array-update) Several sediment-velocity interpolants leave nx+1 or ny+1 entries untouched except on selected physical boundaries, yet full-array magnitudes and transports consume those entries.

claim: [L2943-L2967] (HIGH/dry-cell division) Turbulence updates divide by hh over unmasked interior ranges, allowing dry cells to generate invalid values.
other_wording: [L2873-L2881, L2943-L2967] (MED/depth-division) The turbulence update divides by hh over active loop ranges without an explicit wet/depth guard, relying on an upstream depth floor.

claim: [L2321-L2327] (HIGH/wrong directional condition) The negative y-slope Nielsen branch tests dzbdx<0 instead of dzbdy<0, so many negative y slopes bypass correction.
other_wording: [L2321-L2327] (HIGH/wrong-component-mask) The negative-slope branch for y-direction Nielsen correction tests dzbdx<0 instead of dzbdy<0, skipping or misapplying the alongshore slope correction.

claim: [L411-L420] (MED/boolean precedence) The bed-slope magnitude condition applies the non-berm mask only to the Svb alternative, so any nontrivial Sub is modified even where bermslopeindexbed is true.
other_wording: [L413-L419] (MED/operator-precedence) The bed-slope exclusion applies only to the Svb half of an OR expression, so any nontrivial Sub enters the Soulsby adjustment even where bermslopeindexbed is true.

claim: [L1475-L1483] (MED/unchecked period/depth index) Bore turbulence divides by Tbore and the runup jet indexes nint(istruct) and divides by local hh without bounds or positive-value checks.
other_wording: [L1475-L1484] (MED/division-precondition) Bore turbulence divides by Tbore and the runup jet uses indexed hh in a square-root denominator without local positive guards or index validation.

claim: [L2800-L2807] (HIGH/unguarded bulk concentration division) Bulk McCall-Van Rijn concentration divides qsedu by hu*uu over the whole grid, including dry faces and zero-flow wet faces.
other_wording: [L2799-L2807] (HIGH/division-by-zero) Bulk McCall-Van Rijn concentration is formed as qsedu/(hu*uu) over the whole array without a wet or nonzero-velocity mask.

claim: [L2094-L2103,L2778-L2785] (HIGH/wrong boundary source index) After the smoothing loop, both transport routines set the top boundary from qsedu(i,:) where loop variable i has advanced to nx+1, copying the opposite boundary rather than qsedu(1,:).
other_wording: [L2094-L2104, L2778-L2785] (HIGH/stale-loop-index) Both smoothed bed-load implementations set the top boundary from qsedu(i,:) after the i loop has finished, when i is nx+1, instead of using the top boundary or adjacent cell.

other_wording: [L1170-L1177] (HIGH/whole-array-overwrite) Inside the i,j loop the representative-size update assigns scalar sums to the entire D50top and D90top arrays rather than to (i,j), leaving every cell equal to the last loop cell.

claim: [L464-L490] (HIGH/uninitialized boundary multiplier) pbbedu(nx+1,:) and pbbedv(:,ny+1) are never assigned before whole-array multiplication into Sub/Svb, so boundary transports can consume undefined values even when a zero transport is expected.

[L1593-L1599] (MED/inconsistent dilatancy scaling) Suspended-load critical velocity uses Ucr*(1+sqrt(srfRhee)) while bed load uses Ucr*sqrt(1+srfRhee), an unexplained nonlinear inconsistency for the same Shields correction.

claim: [L290-L356] (MED/reinitialization/configuration lifecycle) nonh_init allocates module arrays unconditionally and never supports cleanup, resizing, or changing nonhq3d mode during a later model lifecycle.
other_wording: [L254-L372] (MED/lifecycle/allocation) nonh_init allocates module work arrays unconditionally, so a second initialization or a grid-size change without an intervening teardown can fail or retain an incompatible module lifecycle.

claim: [L3311-L3319,L3420-L3465] (MED/unbounded/singular dispersion solve) wcoef initialization does not validate Topt, and disper has singular arithmetic for zero frequency/depth plus an iteration with no maximum-count or stagnation guard.
other_wording: [L3453-L3465] (LOW/iteration termination) disper iterates solely on an error tolerance with no iteration cap or invalid-input guard, leaving termination dependent on unstated positive finite inputs.

claim: [L1694-L1720,L1912-L1925,L2546-L2599,L2968-L3031] (HIGH/singular layer-fraction formulas) Reduced-layer formulas divide by 1-wcoef, 2-wcoef sums, and nhlay-nhlay^2 while only checking nhlay>0, so nhlay/wcoef equal or near one makes the system singular.
